preview_en:
Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are two teams adapting to new management having made changes in the summer, with the visitors coming off a massive victory last weekend.

Match News and Current Form

Leverkusen under Carles Martínez Novell remain a work in progress, but Wednesday’s 2-0 UEFA Europa League win over Celje was a momentum-building victory having needed a late equaliser to draw 2-2 with Augsburg last weekend. They ended the last matchday in seventh place with the same record after three games as last term (W1, D1, L1), although they’ve won just one of their last five league fixtures since beating Leipzig here in May (D2, L2). A return to the BayArena may offer encouragement as Die Werkself have only lost one of their last nine home Bundesliga matches (W5, D3).

Despite finishing third last term, Leipzig also changed managers in pre-season and it’s been a wild, goal-filled ride under Martín Demichelis, typified by a 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como before they thrashed Hamburg 5-0 last weekend. The attack-minded Red Bulls ended matchday three in fifth place (W2, L1) with only table-topping Freiburg having scored more than their nine goals, but their defence remains a concern as Leipzig try to avoid losing four consecutive away league games for the first time since a run of five that ended in August 2021.

Head-to-Head History

Leverkusen have scored 2+ goals in each of the last seven H2Hs, failing to win just two of those games (D1, L1). They could now avoid defeat in four Bundesliga matches in a row against Leipzig for the first time, and have won three of the last four clashes they hosted (L1).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Leverkusen have lost just one of their last 30 league games on a Sunday (W19, D10).

Leverkusen won the corner count in each of their last eight home Bundesliga fixtures.

Leipzig have lost just one of their last 16 Sunday-held league games (W12, D3).

Seven of Leipzig’s last eight away league games produced over 2.5 goals with both teams scoring.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Facundo Medina has scored in two of Leverkusen’s last three fixtures, with each of his last four goals coming at home as the second goal of the game. Antonio Nusa has scored three times in five appearances for Leipzig this term and each of his last 11 goals for club and country contributed to victories.

Ibrahim Maza missed Leverkusen’s midweek game with illness, while Leipzig are expected to remain without Christoph Baumgartner , Assan Ouédraogo and Rocco Reitz .

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With Leverkusen strong at home and Leipzig’s recent away games regularly producing goals, backing Leverkusen to win and both teams to score could be worth pursuing.

Author: John Pennington
